about_p1: I learn fastest by breaking things on the bench: a jittery servo that took a PWM rewrite to calm down, a VHDL decoder that passed ModelSim and failed on hardware, or a Celery worker that quietly died overnight. Debugging those taught me to measure early instead of assuming.
about_p2: I also enjoy teaching. Being on the TA team for Electromagnetics (Dr. Askarpour) and Digital Logic Design (Dr. Pourfard) forced me to explain concepts cleanly, which always exposed whatever I hadn't fully understood yet.

int_plain_text: Power-grid SCADA networks are wired directly to high-voltage breakers and substation equipment. A malicious packet can trip a line or damage hardware, so security has to be built into the network architecture from day one.
int_p1: During summer 2026 at Modje Niroo R&D, I studied the full SCADA chain in Iran's power industry: PLCC, industrial Ethernet, serial and fibre links; RTU hardware; the dispatching hierarchy (SCC, AOC, RDC, DAS); the shift to IEC 61850 digital substations; and the domestic Paya-SCADA platform. I documented the work in a 189-page report: “SCADA Architecture and Security in the Iranian Power Industry”.
int_p2: In the lab phase, I tested four detection scenarios on live traffic using Snort, Suricata, OSSEC, and Wazuh:
int_proof_1: DNP3 Deep Packet Inspection: Detected analog point 3 crossing threshold 20 and separated breaker 11 open/close commands in both Snort and Suricata (offline PCAP and live).
int_proof_2: SYN Flood Detection: Caught SYN floods using a 20 packets / 5 seconds behavioral threshold.
int_proof_3: Brute-Force Correlation: Caught 21 consecutive failed login attempts to Paya-SCADA across both network and host layers.
int_proof_4: Event-Rate Anomaly (SID 1000330): Flagged 9–10 events/sec spikes against a normal 15–25s interval, and verified that both DNP3 and WebSocket traffic ran in cleartext.
int_fig_cap: FIG. 1 — Substation-to-dispatch monitoring chain tested in the Modje Niroo lab.
gloss_1_d: Protocols carrying analog measurements and breaker commands between substation RTUs and dispatch centers.
gloss_2_d: Digital substation standard using fast Layer-2 multicast frames (EtherType 0x88B8) for protection events.
gloss_3_d: Custom IDS rule written in the lab to catch sudden SCADA event-rate spikes.
